::: {#rem-halting-in-practice}
#### Undecidability in practice

[Turing machines](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine) can simulate programs in ordinary programming languages
([the Church-Turing thesis](models-of-computation.qmd#rem-church-turing)),
so @thm-halting-undecidable says that no program can check, for every program and input,
whether that program finishes.
A job scheduler that runs users' model-fitting code cannot predict which jobs will loop forever,
so it stops jobs with a time limit instead.
Tools that always finish and check code for infinite loops exist,
but on some programs each one must answer "unknown",
miss a loop,
or flag a program that does [halt](models-of-computation.qmd#def-turing-machine).
The proof that [Kolmogorov complexity](kolmogorov-complexity.qmd#thm-kolmogorov-uncomputable)
cannot be computed is a second example of an uncomputable function,
proved by a different argument.

:::
